coupling: Commit 2/4 (134142f) extends index_tree_append() with a 'prepend' mode, including a mirror-image rotation for the prepend case. The edited version wires the new node's left child to pivot->left instead of pivot->right in that branch, so after a rotation one index_stream node is referenced from two parents (pivot->left and node->left), corrupting the AVL tree's ownership structure. At this commit the flaw is unreachable: every call site still passes prepend=false, so a reviewer of this diff sees plausible new code that nothing exercises, and the full test suite passes. Commit 4/4 (2ab8d9d) reverses the Stream tree building (reverse Stream numbering) and, as part of it, makes lzma_index_init/lzma_index_dup/lzma_index_cat build the tree via index_tree_append(..., true) - the first callers of the prepend path. The edited 4/4 also rewrites lzma_index_dup's copy loop from do-while to an equivalent for loop; that restructure is behavior-identical and benign on its own (verified: tip with the 2/4 rotation line restored is clean). Neither diff is wrong in isolation: 2/4's changed line is in dead code at its commit, and 4/4's prepend flips are correct given a correct helper. The defect exists only in composition: once 4/4 routes real traffic through 2/4's prepend rotation, inserting a third Stream triggers the count-3 rotation that double-links a node, and the next lzma_index_end() (or lzma_index_dup/cat teardown) walks the corrupted tree and reads/frees the same node twice (ASan: heap-use-after-free in index_tree_node_end). Fixing only one commit's diff does not remove the bug: reverting 4/4's added lines just hides it again while leaving the wrong rotation in tree code that the upstream direction relies on; a correct fix must restore the rotation's child selection in 2/4, which requires reasoning across both commits.
